```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r setup}
library(totalevalerror)
```

When LLM call-to-call variability differs across temperatures (e.g., temperature = 0 has near-zero residual variance while temperature = 1.0 has substantial variance), the homoscedastic `lmer` fit pools residuals across strata and biases the replicate-noise component. The package's `heteroscedastic = "stratified"` mode fits a separate `lmer` per temperature stratum and reports per-stratum residual variances.

## Simulate heteroscedastic data

```{r simulate}
# Three temperatures with different residual variances.
sims <- lapply(seq_along(c(0.005, 0.04, 0.08)), function(i) {
  s <- tee_simulate(
    N = 25, V = 3, M = 2, R = 3,
    variances = list(
      item = 0.20, prompt = 0.05,
      item_x_prompt = 0.04, item_x_judge = 0.08,
      cell_level = 0.01,
      replicate = c(0.005, 0.04, 0.08)[i]
    ),
    seed = i
  )
  s$temperature <- factor(c(0, 0.5, 1.0)[i])
  s
})
sim <- do.call(rbind, sims)
```

## Fit homoscedastic (default) vs stratified

```{r fits}
des <- tee_design(
  sim,
  outcome     = outcome,
  item        = item_id,
  prompt      = variant_id,
  judge       = judge_model,
  temperature = temperature,
  replicate   = replication,
  scoring     = "likert"
)

fit_homo  <- suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(
  tee_decompose(des, heteroscedastic = "none")
))
fit_strat <- suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(
  tee_decompose(des, heteroscedastic = "stratified")
))
```

The stratified fit retains per-stratum residual variances:

```{r stratum}
fit_strat$meta$residual_by_temperature
```

The homoscedastic fit reports a single pooled residual that hides the heteroscedasticity:

```{r homo}
fit_homo$variance[fit_homo$variance$tle_label == "replicate noise", ]
```
